To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) positional errors can have a strong impact on the relationships between soil properties and remote sensing data, (ii) positional errors can be estimated by using the GPS measurements of field data, (iii) the interpolation of soil organic carbon contents is more accurate when the positional errors of field observations are taken into consideration, and (iv) the interpolation of the soil organic carbon contents can lead to the identification of fields with low soil fertility.

positional accuracy of the field data can play an important role in soil mapping and that the use of standardized methods to estimate and evaluate the impact of positional accuracy seems to be an efficient way to improve the quality of soil maps.
the positional errors can have an impact on the relationships between soil properties and satellite imagery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of positional errors while estimating the soil organic matter contents in the topsoil using satellite images.
the impact of positional errors in soil organic matter contents mapping using remote sensing and soil sampling data.
the impact of positional errors in the context of remote sensing and soil survey.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the impact of the positional inaccuracies on the interpolation results depends on the interpolation method used and that the use of more advanced methods, such as geostatistical techniques, is recommended.
the use of satellite data for soil mapping should be accompanied by an assessment of the positional accuracy of the field data.
the impact of positioning inaccuracies on the interpolation and mapping of soil organic carbon contents should not be ignored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the positional accuracy of the data is a key parameter that should be considered when using different sources of information to create maps of soil properties.
the positional errors of the field samples can be important and should be considered when using satellite imagery for soil surveying purposes.
the positional accuracy is an important factor to be considered while using remote sensing data and soil organic carbon contents for mapping.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the positional accuracy of the field data should be taken into account when combining different data sources in a spatial analysis.
the positional errors of ground-based observations have to be taken into account in soil mapping studies.
the positional accuracy is important for the quality of the results and should be considered in future work.
